# Nemlig & GrowthBook Commercial Discussion
Date: 2026-10-13 | Duration: 23.780000686645508m

## Summary
Simon and James compared GrowthBook’s experiment-based and unlimited-license pricing against the current AB Tasty, PostHog, and Firebase setup. Simon favored the Launch model starting at $75,000, with unlimited seats and pay-per-experiment pricing, because GrowthBook’s current 22–25-seat structure includes unused licenses and is harder to align with usage. The unlimited model costs $168,750 annually for 25 seats, while AB Tasty costs about 300,000 DKK annually; PostHog and Firebase may create substantially higher costs if usage limits are removed. GrowthBook’s warehouse-native architecture, direct BigQuery data flow, privacy benefits, and centralized experimentation and feature flags were important advantages. Mobile experimentation, especially for iOS, is a key requirement, although some session replay capabilities may remain with PostHog. Simon wants a business case showing potential revenue impact, including modeling based on 60% of 3.3 billion DKK revenue from apps, a typical 0.1% conversion lift, and a 25% test-success rate. James offered migration support, a 10% first-year discount for signing before October 28th, and contract preparation. Leadership discussions were expected after the holiday week, with a Wednesday follow-up planned.

## Keywords
pricing, experimentation, AB Tasty, GrowthBook, data privacy, mobile app testing

## Action Items

**James Shannon**
Send Simon contract template reflecting experiment-based pricing for internal legal review (20:07)
Provide detailed pricing numbers and model breakdown to Simon to facilitate internal financial discussion (16:45)
Follow up with Simon on Wednesday for decision update and next steps (20:35)
Assist with transition from self-hosted GrowthBook to cloud-based solution (09:03)

**Simon Boriis**
Provide James with internal numbers and data needed to finalize pricing proposal and business case (16:45)
Initiate internal discussions post-holiday to evaluate GrowthBook proposal and pricing options (07:51)
Review and coordinate with legal team regarding contract template once received (19:10)

# Nemlig & GrowthBook Catchup
Date: 2026-10-21 | Duration: 16.290000915527344m

## Summary
The discussion evaluated replacing or consolidating Wingify and GrowthBook Pro with one GrowthBook Enterprise platform, using pricing, feature coverage, implementation timing, and team adoption as the main criteria. GrowthBook supports widgets and pop-ups through Figma designs imported into its Visual Editor and is expected to support A/B testing at least as well as the current tooling, but surveys would require PostHog, in-house development, or coded surveys attached to feature flags. It was viewed as stronger for data ownership and potentially less complex for GDPR and legal requirements, while mobile testing remains unresolved. James proposed an Enterprise package priced at 56,000, including full support, app testing, and a six-month invoice deferral. Approval is needed from senior leadership by the end of the month. Simon described migration as a small task involving exporting the current setup and redirecting the front end to a new cluster. Casper planned to review the proposal with Simon and leadership, with a response expected by the beginning to middle of the following week. James would send a template contract to accelerate execution.

## Keywords
GrowthBook, Wingify, A/B testing, app experimentation, contract overlap, GDPR

## Action Items
**Casper von Staffeldt**
- Discuss GrowthBook proposal (13:56)

**James Shannon**
- Prepare template contract (14:21)
